styles.name: Modern Minimal
styles.blurb: Plain fabrics, hidden hardware and daylight doing the decorating — the blind should almost disappear when it is up.

palette.line: Chalk white carries every window, pale grey takes the ones facing the street, and graphite appears once — on the chain and the brackets.

mistake_one.title: Paying for a cassette you do not need
mistake_one.body: A cassette headbox is sold as the tidy finish for a plain blind, and on a recessed window it hides nothing — the fabric already disappears into the reveal. It adds a third to the price and a plastic box to a window that was meant to be empty.
mistake_one.fix: Order a bare roller with a fascia-free bracket, and put the saving into a better fabric.

styles.name: Warm Scandinavian
styles.blurb: Pale wood, soft linen and light kept warm rather than blocked — a window that looks good empty and better half-drawn.

palette.line: Warm white is the wall behind every blind, oatmeal linen is the fabric, light oak is the slat, and clay turns up once — a single cushion, never a blind.

mistakes.setup: That one is the cheapest of the five to put right. The other four are ranked by what they cost to undo, and the one that costs most is
mistakes.trigger: the wood tone, matched to the wrong floor,

materials.setup: Linen and pale oak agree on almost everything, and the one thing they do not is
materials.trigger: a bright white lining, which reads as cold,

shopping.trigger: ordering all the windows at once,

mistake_one.title: Buying "linen" that is not linen
mistake_one.body: Most blinds sold as linen are a polyester weave printed to look like it, and they hang like it too: stiff folds, a shine in side light, and a colour that goes grey rather than mellowing. The word costs nothing to print on a label.
mistake_one.fix: Ask for the fibre content in writing, and accept a linen-cotton blend before a polyester that only borrows the name.

styles.name: Classic Elegant
styles.blurb: Weight, lining and a proper pole — blinds that are part of the room's furniture, not a fitting on the glass.

palette.line: Cream ground keeps the room from going heavy, forest velvet is the blind itself, walnut is the pole, and aged brass appears only on the finials and the hold-back.

mistakes.setup: That one is the cheapest of the five to put right. The other four are ranked by what they cost to undo, and the one that costs most is
mistakes.trigger: the lining, chosen after the fabric,

materials.setup: Velvet and brass carry a room on their own, and the pairing that turns the whole thing to costume is
materials.trigger: a printed damask beside a real one,

shopping.setup: Measure the drop before the width, because with {light} in the picture the one number people get wrong is
shopping.trigger: where the blind stacks when it is up,

dna.setup: Every price band in this category has a "luxury" line, and the trap is that the word is doing the work — the first one is
dna.trigger: a made-to-measure price for a stock size,

splurge.setup: Spend on the fabric and the lining, save on the pole, and the piece that ages worst is
splurge.trigger: the cheap brass, by the second winter,

mistake_one.title: Choosing the lining last
mistake_one.body: A roman blind is two fabrics, and the one nobody sees decides how it hangs, how much light it stops and whether the face fabric fades. Left to the end it defaults to whatever is cheapest, and a velvet blind with a thin lining is a curtain that cannot make up its mind.
mistake_one.fix: Choose the lining with the fabric, in the same shop, in the same light — blackout for a bedroom, interlined for anything that has to hang heavy.

styles.name: Natural Organic
styles.blurb: Bamboo, jute and stone-coloured weaves — texture over pattern, and every window a little different from the next.

palette.line: Warm plaster is the wall, honey bamboo is the blind, linen stone is the softer fabric on the room it needs to be quiet in, and terracotta is the one thing that is allowed to be loud.

mistakes.setup: That one is the cheapest of the five to put right. The other four are ranked by what they cost to undo, and the one that costs most is
mistakes.trigger: the weave that lets the whole street in,

materials.setup: Bamboo and linen live together easily, and the one combination that goes straight to holiday rental is
materials.trigger: two woven blinds in two different tones,

shopping.setup: Buy the living room first and the bathroom last, because with {material} in the picture the mistake is
shopping.trigger: a natural weave in the one room that steams,

dna.setup: The trap in this category is that texture photographs well, so the first thing you pay for is
dna.trigger: a lining you were never told about,

splurge.setup: Spend on one real woven-wood blind where the light hits it, save everywhere else, and the thing that gives a cheap one away is

mistake_one.title: A woven blind with no privacy
mistake_one.body: A bamboo or jute weave looks solid in the shop and turns into a lantern at night: with the lights on, every gap in the weave shows the room to the street. It is the most common reason a natural blind gets taken down within a year.
mistake_one.fix: Order a privacy lining on any woven blind facing a road, or pair it with a sheer roller behind it for the evenings.

styles.name: Bold Statement
styles.blurb: Black slats, charcoal fabric and steel-framed windows — the blind is a graphic element, and it is meant to be seen.

palette.line: Charcoal is the fabric, matte black is the slat and the hardware, steel grey is where the light lands, and red brick is the wall that stops it all reading as a cinema.

mistakes.setup: That one is the cheapest of the five to put right. The other four are ranked by what they cost to undo, and the one that costs most is
mistakes.trigger: the black that is not the same black,

materials.setup: Black metal and dark fabric want one warm surface between them, and the pairing that never works is
materials.trigger: gloss black slats against matte black frames,

shopping.setup: Order the largest window first, because with {slats} in the picture the number people get wrong is
shopping.trigger: the slat width, not the drop,

dna.setup: Dark blinds are where retailers hide the biggest markups, because black shows nothing in a photograph — the first trap is
dna.trigger: the "designer" black at twice the price,

splurge.setup: Spend on the metal venetian you see from the sofa, save on every blackout roller, and the look breaks on
splurge.trigger: a white chain on a black blind,

mistake_one.title: Mixing blacks
mistake_one.body: There are warm blacks, blue blacks and grey blacks, and a black venetian beside a black steel window frame in a different one looks like a mistake from across the room. It is the single most visible error in a dark scheme and the one nobody can name.
mistake_one.fix: Take a slat sample to the window frame in daylight before you order, and match the hardware to the frame, not to the fabric.

mistakes.brief: The five buying mistakes people with this style make with blinds: wrong type for the room, wrong measurement, wrong lining, wrong control side, wrong finish. Each expensive to undo once the brackets are in.

palette.intro: A {name} window palette works on three colours and a strict split: one quiet fabric doing the bulk, one carrying the slats or the lining, and one appearing rarely enough to still register.
palette.closing_rule: Keep every blind in the same room to one fabric family, and let the hardware, never the fabric, carry the second finish.

items.title: Measuring the width first
items.body: Every blind is quoted by width, so that is the number people measure and the drop gets guessed. A blind that stops short of the sill looks unfinished, and one that pools on it wears out at the hem within a year.
items.fix: Measure the drop at both sides and the middle, and order to the longest.

items.title: One control side for the whole house
items.body: The chain or the wand goes where the fitter puts it, and on a window beside a wardrobe or a tap that is the wrong side for the rest of the blind's life. Nobody notices until the first morning.
items.fix: Stand at each window and decide which hand reaches it before you order.

items.title: Skipping the lining question
items.body: A blind is two layers and the one nobody looks at decides the light, the privacy and how the face fabric ages. Left to the default it is whatever is cheapest.
items.fix: Name the lining you want on the order — blackout, privacy or none — and check it is on the confirmation.

items.title: Paying for a motor on a window you never touch
items.body: Motorisation is sold on the biggest window and used on it least. The budget that went on the motor is the budget the bedroom blackout needed.
items.fix: Motorise only the blind you would otherwise reach over furniture for.

items.title: Ordering every window at once
items.body: The first blind up teaches you the mount, the control side and the fabric in the room's own light. Ordering all of them from a swatch skips that lesson and pays for it in returns.
items.fix: Order one, hang it, live with it for a week, then order the rest.

materials.intro: In a {name} home the blind type matters more than the fabric, because the type decides how the window looks when the blind is up as well as down.

pairs.combo: Plain roller with a matching fascia
pairs.why: The fascia hides the roll and the blind disappears when raised, which is the whole point of a plain fabric.

pairs.combo: Wooden venetian with cotton ladder tapes
pairs.why: The tapes hide the cord holes and read as furniture rather than as a fitting, which is what a wooden blind is for.

pairs.combo: Woven-wood shade over a window facing the street, unlined
pairs.why: It is a lantern at night; every gap in the weave shows the room to the pavement.

pairs.combo: Sheer roller under a blackout roman on one bracket
pairs.why: Day and night handled by two blinds on one fitting, and the sheer softens the roman's stack when it is up.

materials.rule: Buy the type for the room's job first — light, privacy, steam — and choose the fabric second.

items.name: Measure every window twice
items.priority_note: Width and drop at three points each, in millimetres, before any catalogue is opened.

items.name: Decide inside or outside the recess
items.priority_note: It changes the size, the light gap and the price, and it cannot be undone after the order.

items.name: Choose the blind type per room
items.priority_note: Blackout for bedrooms, moisture-proof for kitchens and bathrooms, filtering for living rooms.

items.name: Name the lining
items.priority_note: Blackout, privacy or none — written on the order, not assumed.

items.name: Pick the control side per window
items.priority_note: The side your hand reaches without moving furniture.

items.name: Order one blind first
items.priority_note: Hang it, live with it, then order the rest to match.

skip.name: The cassette headbox on a recessed window
skip.why: The reveal already hides the roll; the box adds a third to the price and a plastic edge to the window.

skip.name: Motorisation on a window you can reach
skip.why: It is the biggest single add-on and the one used least.

narrative: The price traps in blinds are words rather than numbers. Made-to-measure on a stock size, designer on a plain fabric, premium on a polyester weave — each one adds to the price and none of them changes what arrives.

For a {name} home the traps cluster around the finish, because a plain or textured blind looks the same in every price band in a photograph and only shows its quality once it has been raised and lowered a few hundred times.
implications: Ask what a label word actually changes in the product before paying for it.
Judge a blind by its mechanism and its lining, not by the name on the fabric.

splurge.item: The one blind you see from where you sit most
splurge.why: That is the window that sets the room, and a real fabric or real wood there carries every cheaper blind in the house.

saves.why: Nobody sees the fabric with the lights off; the coating is what matters and every price band has it.
Moisture-proof faux-wood or a wipeable roller does the job at a third of the price of the real thing.
A bracket in the wrong finish costs pennies to swap; a fabric in the wrong colour costs the whole blind.

splurge.split_note: Put half the whole budget into the main window and split the rest evenly across the others.

stub_colors: Every blind in the main room, and the wall they hang against.
Slats where you have them, linings where you do not.
Chains, brackets and finials, and nothing larger.
One cushion or one blind in one room, never a second.
